identity: Compared with twelve point, K is about 10–14% narrower while L is about 17–21% wider in 1897 and census specimens at thresholds 185/205. The recurring cross-book differences also distinguish ten point from the smaller cuts.
visual_review: All 37 visible native crops and final silhouettes reviewed at 185 and 32 pixels, and words at 16/24/40/64/96 pixels. Four final trial sheets, seven threshold sheets, all native cross-book comparisons and the full 36-character twelve-point comparison inspected. The complete figure 4 diagonal, figure 6/8/9 bowls, Q/R tails and serif terminals are retained.
source_choices: Census A–Y except R supply the capitals; R/Z and figures 1–8 use matching 1897 impressions. The census supplies 0/9 absent from the 1897 sample. The period is doc10-26. Four source books are retained, with three supplying traced forms.
rejected_trials: The initial general threshold 200 added excess scan fringe. Most capitals now use 175, with individual thresholds 185/195 where needed to preserve the printed terminals and serifs.

Lower thresholds shorten the B foot and Q tail. Figure 4 loses its diagonal at 175, figure 6 loses its bowl join at 175, figure 8 loses bowl joins at 175, and census 9 remains open at 185. Figure 2 needs 195 for the fuller foot terminal and figure 7 for its left beak.
geometry: Uniform measured cap scale and rigid source-row rotation. Separate figure groups use local baselines from 1/4/7 at the same physical scale. No independent width fitting, hole filling or drawn replacement strokes.
native_limitations: Minor printed irregularities remain, including the H crossbar join, small figure 6 terminal and Q tail. The recorded outline follows the selected native evidence without analytic repairs.
